stem:
A 19-year-old man who is 193 cm tall presents to the emergency department with sudden right-sided pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath after bench-pressing. Vital signs are stable. Examination shows diminished breath sounds, hyperresonance, and reduced chest expansion on the right. Chest radiography shows complete collapse of the right lung with a visible pleural line and no mediastinal shift.

Which of the following best explains why voluntary inspiration fails to reinflate the affected lung?

options.label: A
options.text: Paralysis of the diaphragm prevents any change in thoracic volume
options.misconception: Phrenic nerve injury is being invoked despite an intact inspiratory pump.
options.explanation: Diaphragmatic paralysis reduces ventilation by preventing thoracic expansion; this patient can inspire, but air cannot enter the collapsed lung because the pleural pressure gradient is lost.

options.label: B
options.text: Loss of the subatmospheric pressure gradient required for lung inflation
options.misconception: None; pneumothorax abolishes the pressure gradient that Boyle's law depends on for inflation.
options.explanation: Normally diaphragm contraction enlarges the pleural cavities and lowers their pressure, drawing air in; when air enters the pleural space the lung collapses and that subatmospheric gradient vanishes, so increasing thoracic volume no longer creates the pressure fall needed for inspiration.

options.label: C
options.text: Surfactant deficiency raises alveolar surface tension and prevents expansion
options.misconception: Neonatal respiratory distress mechanism is being applied to traumatic pneumothorax.
options.explanation: Surfactant reduces alveolar surface tension in immature lungs; pneumothorax fails because pleural air eliminates the negative intrapleural pressure that drives inflation, not because of surfactant loss.

options.label: D
options.text: Bronchospasm raises airway resistance above the driving pressure gradient
options.misconception: Obstructive airflow limitation is being substituted for a pleural-space defect.
options.explanation: Bronchospasm impedes airflow through patent airways; complete lung collapse from pneumothorax reflects loss of the pleural pressure gradient, not increased airway resistance alone.

options.label: E
options.text: Alveolar consolidation eliminates compliant tissue on the affected side
options.misconception: Pneumonia-style filling defect is being confused with pleural air.
options.explanation: Consolidation stiffens lung parenchyma but leaves the pleural cavity intact; radiographic pleural line and hyperresonance indicate air in the pleural space, not parenchymal consolidation.

context: Learning objective: apply Boyle's law to pneumothorax. Inspiration requires diaphragmatic expansion to lower pleural and alveolar pressure; pneumothorax equalizes pleural pressure with atmosphere and abolishes the gradient that draws air in.
